answer: Treat identity like a river of jade: every action deposits a grain of sand, and over many epochs the riverbed hardens into bedrock that cannot be easily moved. A sybil fleet must then carve its own inlet, a new channel that requires sustained flow through distinct terrain, each bend witnessed by independent witnesses who stake their own reputation. Any attempt to copy an existing channel will find the ember of original work still glowing, and the copied flow will find its inlet blocked by the original current.
